sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in Round Lake Beach?
sections.html:
Round Lake Beach owners can list on the market, sell privately, or sell directly to a buyer who pays cash. The direct sale is quickest, but every route runs through the village's occupancy permit, which is required before a residential property is sold. Starting that permit at least two weeks before closing keeps the date from slipping.

The sections that follow describe the village, its housing figures and the steps for water service, inspection and recording in Lake County.

  • Listing the house brings the most exposure along with showings and repair requests.
  • Selling it yourself saves the commission and puts the paperwork on you.
  • A direct sale to a cash buyer is usually as-is and closes when you are ready.

sections.h2: What kind of village is Round Lake Beach?
sections.html:
Round Lake Beach is a village in northern Lake County, incorporated on February 5, 1937, and covers about 5.2 square miles. The 2020 census counted 27,252 residents, down from 28,175 in 2010. It is the principal city of the Round Lake Beach, McHenry and Grayslake urban area, which had 261,835 people in 2020, and the village has the second highest Latino population in Lake County after Waukegan.

Population grew from 1,892 in 1950 to 25,859 in 2000, so the housing stock reflects building over several decades. Major streets include Monaville Road, Fairfield Road, Rollins Road, Cedar Lake Road, Hook Drive and Hainesville Road.

The village spends roughly $3 million to $4 million a year on infrastructure improvements using tax increment financing and motor fuel tax money, according to Wikipedia.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Round Lake Beach homes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts estimates the population at 26,902 on July 1, 2025, down 1.3% from the 2020 base. From 2020 to 2024 it counts 8,537 households averaging 3.16 people, and 79.3% of housing units are owner-occupied.

At a median value of $199,200, a house here sells at a lower price point than in many Chicago suburbs, so the cost of a new roof or furnace weighs more heavily against the sale price.

sections.h2: How do commuting and jobs affect demand in Round Lake Beach?
sections.html:
The village has a station on Metra's North Central Service, which runs between Antioch and Chicago Union Station on weekdays. Pace Route 570 connects Round Lake Beach with Fox Lake, Grayslake and other points. Census data puts the mean commute at 30.4 minutes, and 72.9% of residents 16 and older are in the labor force.

The train station and the road links along Rollins Road and Cedar Lake Road are the usual selling points for a commuter. Households here are large, at 3.16 people each, so family-sized houses are the norm.

sections.h2: Which school district serves Round Lake Beach?
sections.html:
Round Lake Area School District 116 serves the village and four other communities. The district reports about 6,000 students, 10 schools and roughly 1,000 staff members, with a four-year graduation rate of 88% for 2024. Round Lake High School reopened in 2016 after a renovation that added 27 learning lab classrooms, science labs and a new gymnasium.

The district opened a school-based health center in 2014 in partnership with the Lake County Health Department and runs an in-district preschool program for about 200 students. Families asking about schools usually want to know the attendance boundary for one address, which the district can confirm.

sections.h2: What is the occupancy permit, and when do you need it?
sections.html:
Round Lake Beach requires every residential property to obtain an Occupancy Permit before it is sold. The permit moves water and sewer service from the seller to the buyer and confirms the exterior is maintained and up to code. The village asks you to contact it at least two weeks before closing.

  • Fill out the online occupancy application, select the address and choose the Occupancy permit type.
  • Attach photos of the water meter.
  • After the application is accepted, pay the $60 fee by emailed link.
  • The inspection is scheduled after payment. It covers the exterior only, and no one has to be present.
  • Five days before closing, email a photo of the inside meter reading and the outside receiver reading, if there is one, so the final water bill can be calculated.

The village's FAQs add that the final water bill must be paid before the buyers can pick up the occupancy certificate. Call the Finance Department at 847-546-2351 as soon as the closing date is set.

sections.h2: How do water bills and deposits work during a sale?
sections.html:
Water and sewer bills go out every two months, in January, March, May, July, September and November, and a bill unpaid after its due date can carry a 10% late fee under the village FAQ. New owners pay a $100 deposit billed on the first bill, refundable only after ownership or tenancy changes and the final bill is paid in full.

The village's billing page lists its water and sewer charges per 1,000 gallons plus per-bill customer and sewer fees, and it adds a phosphorus surcharge for regional treatment at the Fox Lake facility. Rates have been adjusted in 2026, so ask Village Hall for the schedule that applies to your final bill.

sections.h2: What if the house is a rental?
sections.html:
Rental owners follow a separate annual certification program. Landlords receive a notice in early to mid October with their inspection times, deadlines and fees. Requirements include a submitted application, the certification fee, a passed inspection with deficiencies resolved, current Crime Free certification, and no outstanding liens or payments owed to the village. Missing the deadline brings a $100 late fee and a two-week extension, and after that the property can go to adjudication with an additional $1,500 fine and liens.

Landlords new to the village must attend a Crime-Free Housing seminar, or show proof of certification from another Chicagoland municipality. Call 847-546-2351 for seminar information. A seller with tenants should confirm the certification is current before accepting a contract.

sections.h2: What transfer taxes and property tax dates apply in Round Lake Beach?
sections.html:
The Lake County Clerk's Recording Division collects the state and county transfer taxes at recording: 50 cents per $500 for the state and 25 cents per $500 for the county, issued as a single stamp. The county's pamphlet says the tax may be paid by buyer or seller, so check your contract. A state transfer declaration (PTAX-203) accompanies the deed unless an exemption statement is signed. The Recording Division is at 18 N County St, 6th Floor, Waukegan, phone 847-377-2575.

The county's list of communities that require their own transfer stamp names Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa and North Chicago. Round Lake Beach is not on it, though you should confirm with Village Hall.

Lake County's 2025 tax calendar, payable in 2026, mailed bills May 1 and set the first installment due June 4 and the second due September 4. Those dates have passed, and the county posts each year's calendar on its Treasurer pages.

faqs.q: Do I need an occupancy permit to sell in Round Lake Beach?
faqs.a: Yes. Residential properties must obtain an Occupancy Permit before sale. The fee is $60 and the inspection covers the exterior only.

faqs.q: How early should I start the permit?
faqs.a: At least two weeks before closing. The village also schedules the final water reading about 3 to 5 days before closing, so call the Finance Department at 847-546-2351 once the date is set.

faqs.q: Does anyone need to be home for the inspection?
faqs.a: No. The occupancy inspection is exterior only, and the village says no one is required to be present.

faqs.q: What is the water deposit for new owners?
faqs.a: A $100 deposit billed on the buyer's first water and sewer bill. It is not refundable until the property changes ownership or tenancy and the final bill is paid in full.

faqs.q: Which office records a Round Lake Beach deed?
faqs.a: The Lake County Clerk's Recording Division in Waukegan. It collects the state and county stamps and records the stamped deed.
